# Jubilees Chapter 34 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** The Amorite war; Joseph sold to Egypt; death of Isaac

---

**34:1** In the sixth year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee, Jacob and all his sons went and settled in the land east of Shechem.

**34:2** The seven Amorite kings gathered against Jacob and his sons to kill them, drawing their swords. Jacob's sons prevailed over them and killed them in the hill country of Shechem. They seized all their herds and all their possessions.

**34:3** Judah killed Mahalath, Dan killed his king, Naphtali killed Hazor, Gad killed Phineas, Asher killed Boaz king of Betoron, Zebulun killed his king, and Reuben killed his king.

**34:4** They killed these seven kings and took all their possessions and grew great in wealth. They gathered the spoil in the city of Shechem.

**34:5** In the seventh year of that week, Joseph went to Dothan to find his brothers. He did not find them in Dothan but went east to Shechem and found them there.

**34:6** His brothers saw him and plotted to kill him. Judah said: "Let us sell him to the Ishmaelites who are passing." They agreed.

**34:7** The Midianite merchants came past and pulled Joseph out of the pit and sold him to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver. They brought him to Egypt.

**34:8** His brothers killed a young goat and dipped Joseph's robe in the blood and sent it to their father Jacob.

**34:9** Jacob mourned Joseph deeply and said: "A wild beast has devoured him." He tore his garments and put on sackcloth and mourned Joseph for many days.

**34:10** Rebekah's nurse Deborah died and Jacob buried her under the oak near Bethel and called the place the Oak of Weeping.

**34:11** In the forty-fifth jubilee, fifth week, first year, Jacob sent Judah to his father Isaac, and Isaac strengthened him. Jacob rejoiced before his father Isaac, and Jacob's sons loved Isaac greatly.

**34:12** When Isaac fell ill, his two sons Esau and Jacob came to him. He was comforted and said: "The days of my years are complete — one hundred and eighty years."

**34:13** In the sixth week, first year, of the forty-fifth jubilee, Isaac died at a very great age. His two sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

**34:14** Esau went to the land of Edom in the mountains of Seir and settled his sons there. Jacob remained at Mamre opposite Hebron.

**34:15** Jacob's sons each returned to their wives and fathered sons and daughters. They were twelve in all, including Benjamin.

**34:16** Reuben's sons: Enoch, Phallu, Hezron, Carmi — four. Simeon's sons: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar — five. Levi's sons: Gershon, Kohath, Merari — three. Judah's sons: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, Zerah — five.

**34:17** In the second year of the sixth week, famine struck all the land except Egypt. Jacob sent his sons, except Benjamin, to buy grain from Egypt.

**34:18** Joseph had become ruler over all Egypt. He was master of all Pharaoh's storehouses, and he was thirty years old when he came before Pharaoh.

**34:19** When Jacob's sons came to Egypt, Joseph recognized them, but they did not recognize him.

**34:20** Joseph commanded: "Bring your younger brother to me." And he kept Simeon with him until they returned with his brother Benjamin.

---

*LOGOS notes: The Amorite war (vv.1-4) is found also in the Testament of Judah 3-7 and likely derives from a common source. Chapter 34 compresses the Joseph material from Genesis 37-42 significantly. The death of Isaac is dated precisely here, as is the famine.*
